questions.q: If& $\sin^{- 1}\text{x} + \sin^{- 1}\text{y} = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$~and~$\cos^{- 1} \text{x} - \cos^{- 1} \text{y} = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$.Then, $( x, y )$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given,

$\sin^{- 1}\text{x} + \sin^{- 1}\text{y} = \dfrac{2\pi}{3} . . . ( i )$

and~$\cos^{- 1}\text{x} - \cos^{- 1}\text{y} = \dfrac{π}{3} . . . ( ii )$

We know that~$\sin^{- 1}\text{x} + \cos^{- 1}\text{x} = \dfrac{π}{2}$

Using the above concept, we can write~

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \sin^{- 1} \text{x}\right) - \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \sin^{- 1} \text{y}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

$⇒ - \sin^{- 1}\text{x} + \sin^{- 1}\text{y} = \dfrac{π}{3} . . . ( iii )$~

On adding equation~ \left(i\right)$ and \left(iii\right)$, we get

$\sin^{- 1} \text{y} = \dfrac{\pi}{2} ⇒ \text{y} = 1$

On subtracting equation \left(i\right)$~from equation~ \left(iii\right)$, we get

$\sin^{- 1} \text{x} = \dfrac{\pi}{6} ⇒ \text{x} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$∴ \left(\text{x, y}\right) = $\$left(\dfrac{1}{2} \text{,}1\right)$

$

questions.solution:
Given,

$f \left(x\right) = {cosec}^{- 1} \left[$1 + \sin^{2}x\right],$~where~\left[\cdot\right]~denotes the greatest integer function.

Since,~

$- 1 ≤ sinx ≤ 1$

$⇒ 0 $\le \sin^{2}$x ≤ 1$

$⇒ 1 ≤ 1 + \sin^{2}x ≤ 2$

$⇒ \left[$1 + \sin^{2}x\right] = 1, 1 $\le \sin^{2}$x < 2$~and

\left[1 + \sin^{2}x\right] = 2, if2 \le 1 + \sin^{2}x < 3$.

So,

$f \left(x\right) = {cosec}^{- 1} \left($1\right)$

$⇒ $f\left($x\right) = $\dfrac{π}{2}

And,

$f \left($x\right) = {cosec}^{- 1}2$

$⇒ $f\left($x\right) = {cosec}^{- 1}2$

Therefore,~f\left($x\right)$~has two values

\left$\${\dfrac{π}{2}, {cosec}^{- 1}$2\right\}$

questions.q: If the value of the expression $tan ⁡ \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\cos^{- 1} ⁡ \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\right)$ is in the form of $a + \sqrt{b}$ where $a, b \in Z,$ then the value of $\dfrac{a + b}{b}$ is K, Find 10K.
questions.solution:
We know that,

$tan ⁡ \left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1 - cos ⁡ x}{sin ⁡ x}$

$∴ tan ⁡ \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\cos^{- 1} ⁡ \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\right) = \dfrac{1 - cos ⁡ \left(\cos^{- 1} ⁡ \left(\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\right)\right)}{sin ⁡ \left(\cos^{- 1} ⁡ \left(\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\right)\right)}$

$= \dfrac{1 - 2 / \sqrt{5}}{sin ⁡ \left(\sin^{- 1} ⁡ \left(1 / \sqrt{5}\right)\right)}$

$= \dfrac{1 - 2 / \sqrt{5}}{1 / \sqrt{5}} = \sqrt{5} - 2$

Now, $a + \sqrt{b} = - 2 + \sqrt{5}$

$⇒ a = - 2$ and $b = 5$

Hence, $\dfrac{a + b}{b} = \dfrac{3}{5} = 0.6$

As we know, $\sinh ^{-1} x=\log x+\sqrt{1+x^2}$ So, $2 \sin \mathrmh^{-1} x=2 \log \left(x+\sqrt{1+x^2}\right)\begin{aligned} & =\log \left(x+\sqrt{1+x^2}\right)^2 \\ & =\log \left[x^2+1+x^2+2 x \sqrt{1+x^2}\right] \\ & 2 \sin \mathrmh^{-1} x=\log \left[2 x^2+1+2 x \sqrt{1+x^2}\right] \end{aligned}$ Now, put $x=\frac{a}{\sqrt{1-a^2}}\begin{aligned} & =\log \left[\frac{2 a^2}{1-a^2}+1+\frac{2 a}{\sqrt{1-a^2}} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-a^2}}\right] \\ & =\log \left[\frac{2 a^2}{1-a^2}+1+\frac{2 a}{1-a^2}\right] \\ & =\log \left[\frac{2 a^2+1-a^2+2 a}{1-a^2}\right] \\ & =\log \left[\frac{a^2+2 a+1}{1-a^2}\right] \\ & \end{aligned}$ Now, by using Eq. (i), $\begin{aligned} & \log \left[\frac{a^2+2 a+1}{1-a^2}\right]=\log \left[\frac{1+x}{1-x}\right] \\ & \frac{a^2+2 a+1}{1-a^2}=\frac{1+x}{1-x} \end{aligned}$ [by using componendo and dividendo rule] $\begin{aligned} & \frac{a^2+2 a+1+1-a^2}{a^2+2 a+1-1+a^2} \\ & =\frac{1+x+1-x}{1+x-1+x} \Rightarrow \frac{2+2 a}{2 a^2+2 a}=\frac{1}{x} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{2(1+a)}{2 a(1+a)}=\frac{1}{x} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{a}=\frac{1}{x} \Rightarrow x=a \end{aligned}$

questions.q: The value of $\cos  \left(2 \cos ^{-1} x+\sin ^{-1} x\right)$ at x=\frac{1}{5}, where $0 \leq \cos ^{-1} x \leq \pi$ and -\frac{\pi}{2} \leq \sin ^{-1}$x \leq \frac{\pi}{2}, is$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \cos \left(2 \cos ^{-1} x+\sin ^{-1} x\right)=\cos \left(\cos ^{-1} x+\cos ^{-1} x+\sin ^{-1} x\right) \\ & =\cos \left(\cos ^{-1} x+\frac{\pi}{2}\right) \quad\left[\because \cos ^{-1} x+\sin ^{-1} x=\frac{\pi}{2}\right] \\ & =-\sin \left(\cos ^{-1} x\right) \\ & =-\sin \left(\sin ^{-1} \sqrt{1-x^2}\right) \\ & =-\sqrt{1-x^2} \\ & =-\sqrt{1-\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^2} \quad\left[\because x=\frac{1}{5}\right] \\ & =-\frac{2 \sqrt{6}}{5}\end{aligned}$

Given that,
$\begin{aligned} & \cot \left(\cos ^{-1} x\right)=\sec \left\{\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{a}{\sqrt{b^2-a^2}}\right)\right\} \\ & \text { Since, } \cos ^{-1} x=\cot ^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\right) \\ & \quad \text { and } \tan ^{-1} x=\sec ^{-1}\left(\sqrt{1+x^2}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \cot \left(\cot ^{-1} \frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\right)=\sec \\ & \left\{\sec ^{-1} \sqrt{1+\left(\frac{a}{\sqrt{b^2-a^2}}\right)^2}\right\} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}=\sqrt{\frac{b^2-a^2+a^2}{b^2-a^2}} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}=\frac{b}{\sqrt{b^2-a^2}}\end{aligned}$
On squaring both the sides, we get
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{x^2}{1-x^2}=\frac{b^2}{b^2-a^2} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad x^2 b^2-x^2 a^2=b^2-b^2 x^2 \\
& \quad x^2 b^2+b^2 x^2-x^2 a^2=b^2 \\
& \quad 2 x^2 b^2-x^2 a^2=b^2 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad x^2\left(2 b^2-a^2\right)=b^2 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad x=\frac{b}{\sqrt{2 b^2-a^2}}
\end{aligned}$

questions.solution: Given, $y=\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{1+a^2 x^2}-1}{a x}\right)\begin{aligned} & \text { put } a x=\tan \theta \Rightarrow \theta=\tan ^{-1}(a x) \\ & y=\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{\sec \theta-1}{\tan \theta}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \quad y=\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{1-\cos \theta}{\sin \theta}\right)=\tan ^{-1} \tan \frac{\theta}{2}=\frac{\theta}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad y=\frac{1}{2} \tan ^{-1}(a x) \Rightarrow y^{\prime}=\frac{1}{2} \frac{a}{1+a^2 x^2} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad\left(1+a^2 x^2\right) y^{\prime}=\frac{a}{2} \Rightarrow\left(1+a^2 x^2\right) y^{\prime \prime}+2 a^2 x y^{\prime}=0 \\ & \therefore \quad g(x)=2 a^2 x \Rightarrow 1+a^2 x^2+g(x)=0 \\ & a^2 x^2+2 a^2 x+1=0 \\ & \text { Sum of roots }=\frac{-2 a^2}{a^2}=-2\end{aligned}$

(i) and (iii), we get $2 a=\frac{n \pi^2}{4} \text { or } 2 a=\frac{2 \pi^2}{4} \quad(\because n=2)$ or $\quad a=\frac{\pi^2}{4} \Rightarrow \cos ^{-1} x=\frac{\pi^2}{4} \Rightarrowx=\cos \left(\frac{\pi^2}{4}\right) Now, from Eq. questions.solution:
Given that,

$2\tan^{- 1}\dfrac{1}{5} + \sec^{- 1}\dfrac{5\sqrt{2}}{7} + 2\tan^{- 1}\dfrac{1}{8}$

$= 2\tan^{- 1}\dfrac{1}{5} + 2\tan^{- 1}\dfrac{1}{8} + \sec^{- 1}\dfrac{5\sqrt{2}}{7}$

$= 2\left(\tan^{- 1}\dfrac{1}{5} + \tan^{- 1}\dfrac{1}{8}\right) + \sec^{- 1}\dfrac{5\sqrt{2}}{7}$

$= 2\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{\dfrac{1}{5} + \dfrac{1}{8}}{1 - \dfrac{1}{5} \cdot \dfrac{1}{8}}\right) + \sec^{- 1}\dfrac{5\sqrt{2}}{7}$

\left∴ \tan^{- 1}A + \tan^{- 1}B = \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{A + B}{1 - AB}\right)\right)$

$= 2\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{8 + 5}{40 - 1}\right) + \sec^{- 1}\dfrac{5\sqrt{2}}{7}$

$= 2\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{13}{39}\right) + \sec^{- 1}\dfrac{5\sqrt{2}}{7}$

$= 2\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) + \sec^{- 1}\dfrac{5\sqrt{2}}{7}$

$= \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{2 \times \dfrac{1}{3}}{1 - \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)2}\right) + \sec^{- 1}\dfrac{5\sqrt{2}}{7}$

\left(∴ 2\tan^{- 1}A = \tan^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{2A}{1 - A^{2}}\right)\right)

$= \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{6}{8}\right) + \sec^{- 1}\dfrac{5\sqrt{2}}{7}

$= \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right) + \sec^{- 1}\dfrac{5\sqrt{2}}{7}

$= \tan^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right) + \tan^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{1}{7}\right)

~

$= \tan^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{\dfrac{3}{4} + \dfrac{1}{7}}{1 - \dfrac{3}{4} \cdot \dfrac{1}{7}}\right)$

$= \tan^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{21 + 4}{28 - 3}\right)

$= \tan^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{25}{25}\right)

$= \tan^{- 1} \left($1\right)$

$∴ 2\tan^{- 1}$\dfrac{1}{5} + \sec^{- 1}\dfrac{5\sqrt{2}}{7} +$2\tan^{- 1}\dfrac{1}{8} = $\dfrac{π}{4}$

$

Now,~$\tan^{- 1}\dfrac{4}{5} - \tan^{- 1}\dfrac{1}{7} = p \left(say\right)$

$⇒ p = \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{\dfrac{4}{5} - \dfrac{1}{7}}{1 + \dfrac{4}{5} \cdot \dfrac{1}{7}}\right) = \tan^{- 1} $\$left(\dfrac{23}{39}\right)

Also,~$\tan^{- $1}\dfrac{4}{3} + \tan^{- $1}\dfrac{1}{9} = q \left(say\right)$

questions.q: The set of values of $\alpha$ such that $f: \mathbf{R} \rightarrow  \left[0, $\frac{\pi}{2}\right) defined by $f(x)=\tan ^{-1} \left(x^2+x+\alpha^2\right)$ is onto is$
questions.solution: Let $A=\left\{x: 0 \leq x < \frac{\pi}{2}\right\}$ Since $f: \mathbf{R} \rightarrow A$ is an onto function, therefore, Range of $f=A\Rightarrow 0 \leq f(x) \leq \frac{\pi}{2}$ for all $x \in \mathbf{R}\Rightarrow 0 \leq \tan ^{-1}\left(x^2+x+\alpha^2\right) \leq \frac{\pi}{2}$ for all $x \in \mathbf{R}\Rightarrow \quad 0 \leq x^2+x+\alpha^2 \leq \infty \quad$ for all $x \in \mathbf{R}\Rightarrow \quad x^2+x+\alpha^2 \geq 0 \quad$ for all $x \in \mathbf{R}\Rightarrow \quad 1-4 \alpha^2 \leq 0 \Rightarrow \alpha^2 \geq \frac{1}{4}\therefore \quad \left(-\infty,$-\frac{1}{2}\right) \cup\left(\frac{1}{2}, \infty\right)
